scientific_evidence: An explicit global nonnegative delay-mass identity, a complete bounded-entire scalar delay argument, and an exact stable equilibrium above threshold support the claim. The symbolic checker verifies identities and the example but does not certify the global theorem.
scientific_limitations: The t^-1 coefficient requires beta=d, r>b+alpha/m, strictly positive current populations, continuous nonnegative initial histories, constant finite gestation delays, and positive model coefficients. Predator extinction for beta<=d does not require the prey-growth margin. No complete beta>d classification or time-varying/stochastic/spatial extension is asserted.
scientific_summary: For the positive three-species delay food chain, both predators die out for beta<=d with arbitrary finite nonnegative delays. At beta=d and r>b+alpha/m, t*x2(t) converges to (r-b)(1+d*tau1)/(a*d*m); above the threshold a stable positive intermediate-predator equilibrium exists for admissible parameters.
title: Critical \(t^{-1}\) predator extinction with an exact gestation-delay factor
